body: I installed via the unstable PPA, and reverted to the stable branch to be able to keep getting work done. Would I have to clone and build to be able to do what you're describing?

Yes. I can't reproduce the issue, so someone with GNOME Terminal needs to try reverting https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/9143 or bisecting.

Does CTRL-L (or `:mode`) fix the display?

`:mode` fixes the view of the current file, but if I change tabs again, it stops working again.

CTRL-L opens new tabs for me in the NetRW view, so it's unclear whether it fixes things for the tab that I'm on.

 in my case, it is reproducible only for the files in a nested directory

I got a local install going, and it does seem like #9143 is the issue. The commit just prior to that is fine, and that commit exhibits the behavior that I'm describing in the issue.

I'm not sure how to debug beyond that, though.

I'm having display issues too, and usually ctrl-l fixes everything. I'm not using netrw, it happens e.g. when closing or navigating tabs, but it doesn't happen always, so I still  haven't understood exactly why or when it happens.

I'm using kitty on macos and the problem appeared after I compiled nvim with #9143
Probably a `redraw_all_later(NOT_VALID)` is done somewhere in the context of the old tab which needs to be moved to the new tab. I'll look into it.

I cannot reproduce, neither with netrw or with some manual testing. Netrw is huge, and its behavior depends on external factors. A simple reproduce with `-u NONE` and only builtin functionality would be helpful.

@bfredl I can't seem to make it happen with `-u NONE`. I was able to get it without NetRW, but that was with my full `nvimrc`. Would it help to have a paste of that? I use enough plugins that it might not be...

@bfredl I suspect it might be some sort of race condition with timers and / or jobs. I wasn't unable to reproduce it with `vim -u NONE`, but while using it normally a couple of times the screen was updated like a second later after closing the tab. this thing plus the randomness of the bug makes me think about something asynchronous.

btw the last time I saw the bug, the tab bar at the top and the status line at the bottom where updated correctly, it was just the content of the tabs / splits that wasn't updated at all

issue.body:
`redraw_all_later()` isn't guaranteed to update `must_redraw` after switching tab, we must do it ourselves.

fixes #9152. Added test fails on master.
